intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that MEHMO syndrome (MEHMO) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the EIF2S3 gene (300161) on chromosome Xp22.11.

checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis indicated that all patients carried a hemizygous mutation in EIF2S3 located on chromosome X as the most likely disease-relevant change.
checks.explanation: The paper links MEHMO syndrome to hemizygous EIF2S3 mutations.

checks.explanation: Gene location is standard nomenclature; consistent with the linkage region containing EIF2S3.

paragraphs.text: DeLozier-Blanchet et al. (1999) described MEHMO as a new syndrome made up of mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. Skopkova et al. (2017) described MEHMO as a rare X-linked syndrome characterized by profound intellectual disability, epilepsy, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. They linked it to mutations in EIF2S3, which encodes the gamma subunit of translation initiation factor eIF2, and placed it among disorders of translation initiation and the integrated stress response.

Brain MRI showed a thin corpus callosum and enlarged lateral ventricles. The parents I.1 and I.2 were first cousins.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) reported a Slovak boy (family 1) born to nonconsanguineous parents. Microcephaly was detected prenatally. At birth he had micropenis, cryptorchidism, and peripheral hypertonia. He developed drug-resistant partial complex seizures at 4 months, severe developmental delay, and central obesity. Non-autoimmune insulin-treated diabetes was diagnosed at 10 months. His dysmorphic features included full cheeks, large ears, downturned corners of the mouth, epiblepharon, tapered fingers, and talipes. Brain MRI showed delayed myelination that progressed with acute demyelinating changes and cerebral atrophy. A muscle biopsy showed abnormal mitochondria. Seizures and diabetes control worsened during infections. At 5 years his height was -5 SD and his head circumference was -8.4 SD.

paragraphs.text: Gregory et al. (2019) described 3 affected males from a nonconsanguineous white European family: monozygotic twin brothers (III4, III5) and their maternal cousin (III3). They had severe recurrent hypoglycemia, short stature with GH and TSH deficiencies, and mild learning difficulties. They also had an unusual form of glucose dysregulation that fluctuated between hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and postprandial hyperglycemia. Brain MRI showed variable white matter loss and a small anterior pituitary, with a normal posterior pituitary and stalk. None had severe intellectual disability or microcephaly, and all 3 boys attended mainstream school.

paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) studied the 3 affected males of a Moroccan Jewish family with X-linked intellectual disability and microcephaly. By exome sequencing within the linkage region, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, they identified a hemizygous c.665T-C transition in the EIF2S3 gene (300161), resulting in an ile222-to-thr (I222T) substitution. The mutation cosegregated with the disorder, and female carriers were heterozygous. It was absent from 188 Moroccan Jewish control X chromosomes, dbSNP132, 1000 Genomes, and more than 8,000 ESP alleles. Ile222 lies in the GTP-binding domain and is strictly conserved in animals. In HeLa cells, the I222T mutant pulled down substantially less eIF2-beta than wildtype. Borck et al. (2012) found no additional EIF2S3 mutations when they sequenced all 12 exons in 60 individuals from families with unspecific, potentially X-linked intellectual disability. They suggested that EIF2S3 mutations confer a specific phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) studied affected males from 3 families with MEHMO syndrome: 2 Slovak families and the German family originally reported by Steinmüller et al. (1998). By whole-exome or X-chromosome exome sequencing, they identified the same hemizygous 4-bp deletion in the last exon of EIF2S3 (c.1394_1397delTCAA) in all 3 families. The deletion causes a frameshift (Ile465SerfsTer4) that replaces the last 8 amino acids with 3 different ones. It segregated with the disease, was absent from dbSNP and ExAC, and had a CADD score of 35. Functional studies in a yeast/human chimera and in patient fibroblasts supported pathogenicity.

paragraphs.text: Gregory et al. (2019) studied 3 affected males of a family with hypopituitarism and glucose dysregulation. The boys inherited the variant from their heterozygous mothers, who were sisters, and it originated from the heterozygous maternal grandmother. It segregated in an X-linked recessive manner over 3 generations, was absent from ExAC and gnomAD, and was predicted to be deleterious. paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) expressed myc/His6-tagged human eIF2-gamma carrying the I222T mutation in HeLa cells. The mutant pulled down substantially less endogenous eIF2-beta than wildtype without affecting eIF2-alpha binding, indicating disrupted eIF2 complex integrity. In structural modeling on archaeal aIF2, the corresponding residue lay in the hydrophobic cleft that binds helix alpha-1 of eIF2-beta. Borck et al. (2012) also tested the analogous mutations in yeast eIF2-gamma. V281T impaired eIF2-beta binding without affecting growth, whereas V281K nearly abolished eIF2-beta binding and impaired growth. Both mutations increased GCN4-lacZ expression (2.5- and 40-fold, respectively) and raised the UUG/AUG initiation ratio 2- to 3-fold. Overexpression of eIF2-beta partially suppressed these defects. The authors concluded that the mutation impairs eIF2 integrity, ternary complex function, and start codon fidelity.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) modeled the Ile465SerfsTer4 mutation in a yeast/human eIF2-gamma chimera. It derepressed GCN4-lacZ expression nearly 3-fold and doubled the UUG/AUG initiation ratio, effects comparable to those of the Val281Thr mutation associated with X-linked intellectual disability. These results indicated that the C-terminal mutation impairs eIF2 function. In patient fibroblasts the C-terminally truncated eIF2-gamma protein was produced. In fibroblasts from a family 3 patient, DDIT3 transcript levels were 2.5-fold higher than in controls and CHOP protein was also elevated, indicating activation of the integrated stress response.

paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) studied 3 affected males of a Moroccan Jewish family with an X-linked intellectual disability syndrome that included microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphism. In these males they identified a hemizygous c.665T-C transition in the EIF2S3 gene, resulting in an ile222-to-thr (I222T) substitution. The mutation was found by exome sequencing within the linkage region and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. It cosegregated with the disorder, and female carriers were heterozygous. It was absent from 188 Moroccan Jewish control X chromosomes, dbSNP132, 1000 Genomes, and more than 8,000 ESP alleles. Ile222 lies in the GTP-binding domain and is strictly conserved in animals. Tagged eIF2-gamma carrying I222T and expressed in HeLa cells pulled down substantially less endogenous eIF2-beta than wildtype, without affecting eIF2-alpha binding. In yeast, the analogous mutations impaired eIF2-beta binding, increased GCN4-lacZ expression, and raised the UUG/AUG initiation ratio.

(2017) identified the same hemizygous c.1394_1397delTCAA mutation in the last exon of EIF2S3 in affected males from 3 families with MEHMO syndrome: 2 Slovak families and the German family originally reported by Steinmüller et al. paragraphs.text: Gregory et al. (2019) studied 3 affected males of a nonconsanguineous white European family with hypopituitarism and glucose dysregulation. By X-exome sequencing they identified a hemizygous c.1294C-T transition in the EIF2S3 gene, resulting in a pro432-to-ser (P432S) substitution at a highly conserved residue in the C-terminal domain of eIF2-gamma. The variant was inherited from heterozygous mothers, who were sisters, and segregated in an X-linked recessive manner over 3 generations. It was absent from ExAC and gnomAD. In yeast, the equivalent P490S mutation caused a modest (about 1.7-fold) increase in GCN4-lacZ expression and increased UUG start codon initiation. The authors proposed that the milder loss of function caused by P432S produces a phenotype distinct from classic MEHMO syndrome, without microcephaly, epilepsy, or obesity.
